key_insight: An evidence-aware AI framework integrates heterogeneous drug-safety data into a reusable knowledge resource that improves downstream AI tasks.
clinical_relevance: The resource could support drug-safety research, but the abstract does not establish cancer-specific utility, drug discovery benefits, or improved patient outcomes.
method: Integrate FAERS reports, biomedical literature, clinical trials, and Mass General Brigham electronic health records.
Combine LLM extraction, ontology-based normalization, and cross-source evidence assessment.
Prioritize drug–adverse event relationships using statistical and machine learning methods, ingredient-based inference, and confidence scores.
evidence_signal: The resource contains 11,588 drug nodes and over 2.47 million relationships; downstream evaluations reported better LLM adverse-event synthesis and improved precision and F1 for clinical adverse-event relation extraction.
watch_item: Confidence-scored associations do not establish causality, and the abstract provides no quantitative performance gains or external validation results.
paper_title: AI-Empowered Multimodal Data Integration and Knowledge Discovery for Pharmacovigilance
